rationale:
The selected theorem is not atomic. It joins smoothness of J (i) with a quantitative Legendre bound (ii). Its supplied proof uses five independent obligations: Gram-determinant positivity, smoothness through the Leibniz formula, the Hessian of J at 0 (chain rule along a line plus a one-variable determinant expansion), the operator-norm vs Hilbert-Schmidt comparison, and local uniform continuity of the Hessian. Two of these are generic calculus facts about any C^2 function on a normed space, so they are stated for a type variable E and are reusable.

One correction to the supplied proof is carried into the children. Step 1 cites Matrix.PosDef.det_pos, but Matrix.PosDef, PosSemidef, gram and posSemidef_gram are not imported by GMT.Ch05.Submission (unknown constants at the pin), and accepted candidates never change imports. The child gram_det_pos therefore proves det(I+G)>0 from the same inequality xi^T(I+G)xi >= |xi|^2 using kernel triviality and the intermediate value theorem. Step 6's coordinate trick only worked around instance synthesis at the concrete bilinear-form type. The generic child hessian_local_unif uses the operator norm directly and needs no finite-dimensionality.

Parent proof from the children:
- (i) is integrand_smooth.
- (ii): J is C^2. hessian_local_unif with F=J, x0=0, delta=1/2 gives eps>0 with |D^2J(P)[Q][Q]-D^2J(0)[Q][Q]| <= (1/2)||Q||^2 whenever ||P||=||P-0|| <= eps. By hessian_at_zero and opnorm_sq_le_hs, D^2J(0)[Q][Q] = sum_a ||Q e_a||^2 >= ||Q||^2. Hence D^2J(P)[Q][Q] >= ||Q||^2 - (1/2)||Q||^2 = (1/2)||Q||^2.

subproblems.title: Positivity of det(I + Gram matrix of P e_a)
subproblems.statement:
For all natural numbers n, l and every continuous linear map P : R^n -> R^l (P : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ), let e_a = EuclideanSpace.single a 1 (a in Fin n) be the standard basis of R^n and G = G(P) the real n x n matrix G_{ab} =

. Then det(I_n + G) > 0, where I_n is the identity matrix.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ n ℓ : ℕ, ∀ P : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ, 0 < Matrix.det ((1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) + Matrix.of fun a b : Fin n => inner ℝ (P (EuclideanSpace.single a (1 : ℝ))) (P (EuclideanSpace.single b (1 : ℝ))))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Notation: fix n, l, P. Write G := G(P) and v_a := P e_a. For xi, eta in R^n (functions Fin n -> R), xi . eta = sum_a xi_a eta_a and (M xi)_a = sum_b M_{ab} xi_b.

1. Quadratic form of G. For every xi, xi . (G xi) = sum_a sum_b xi_a <v_a, v_b> xi_b = <sum_a xi_a v_a, sum_b xi_b v_b> = ||P(sum_a xi_a e_a)||^2. This uses bilinearity and symmetry of the real inner product and linearity of P (P(sum_a xi_a e_a) = sum_a xi_a v_a). In particular xi . (G xi) >= 0.

2. Trivial kernel of I + sG for s >= 0. Let s >= 0 and suppose (I + sG) xi = 0. Taking the dot product with xi gives 0 = xi . xi + s xi . (G xi) = sum_a xi_a^2 + s ||P(sum_a xi_a e_a)||^2. Both summands are >= 0 (s >= 0 and step 1), so sum_a xi_a^2 = 0. A sum of squares vanishes only if every term does, so xi = 0.

3. Nonvanishing determinant. For a square matrix M over R, det M = 0 iff M xi = 0 for some xi != 0 (Matrix.exists_mulVec_eq_zero_iff). By step 2, det(I + sG) != 0 for every s >= 0.

4. Continuity. h(s) := det(I + sG) is continuous in s in R: s -> I + sG is continuous entrywise and det is a polynomial in the entries (Continuous.matrix_det). Also h(0) = det I = 1.

5. Intermediate value theorem. Suppose det(I + G) = h(1) <= 0. Then h(1) <= 0 <= 1 = h(0) and h is continuous on [0, 1]. The intermediate value theorem (intermediate_value_Icc') gives s in [0, 1] with h(s) = 0. Since s >= 0, this contradicts step 3. Hence det(I + G) = h(1) > 0. QED

Source: parent step 1. The input is the same inequality xi^T (I + G) xi >= |xi|^2. The conclusion is reached by the continuity argument because Matrix.PosDef, Matrix.PosSemidef, Matrix.PosDef.det_pos, Matrix.gram and Matrix.posSemidef_gram are NOT imported by GMT.Ch05.Submission (checked at the pin: unknown constants), and the Submission imports must stay unchanged.

subproblems.title: The area integrand J is C^infinity
subproblems.statement:
For all natural numbers n, l, with e_a = EuclideanSpace.single a 1 and G(P)_{ab} =

, the function J(P) = sqrt(det(I_n + G(P))) on the normed space L = L(R^n, R^l) (Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ with the operator norm) is C^infinity (ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞)).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ n ℓ : ℕ, ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) (fun P : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ => Real.sqrt (Matrix.det ((1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) + Matrix.of fun a b : Fin n => inner ℝ (P (EuclideanSpace.single a (1 : ℝ))) (P (EuclideanSpace.single b (1 : ℝ))))))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Notation: fix n, l. L := Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ, M(P) := I + G(P) (a real n x n matrix) and D(P) := det M(P). 1. Smooth entries. For fixed a, P -> P e_a is the continuous linear evaluation map L -> R^l at e_a, hence C^infinity. The real inner product is a continuous bilinear map, so P ->

is C^infinity (ContDiff.inner). Adding the constant (I)_{ab}, every entry P -> M(P)_{ab} is C^infinity. 2. Smooth determinant. By the Leibniz formula (Matrix.det_apply), D(P) = sum over permutations sigma of Fin n of sign(sigma) * prod_i M(P)_{sigma(i), i}. A finite product of C^infinity real functions is C^infinity (contDiff_prod). Multiplying by the constant sign(sigma) in {1, -1} preserves C^infinity. A finite sum of C^infinity functions is C^infinity (ContDiff.sum). Hence D is C^infinity on L. 3. Positivity. By the sibling gram_det_pos (Submission.dohr_eb_ail_gram_det_pos), D(P) > 0, in particular D(P) != 0, for every P in L. 4. Square root. If D : L -> R is C^infinity and D(P) != 0 for all P, then P -> sqrt(D(P)) is C^infinity, because sqrt is C^infinity away from 0 (ContDiff.sqrt). Therefore J = sqrt o D is C^infinity on L. QED Source: parent step 2. Lean note (checked at the pin; a complete proof compiled): there is no smoothness lemma for Matrix.det at the pin and Matrix has no global norm instance, so work on scalar entries through the Leibniz formula. - Entries: after `simp only [Matrix.add_apply, Matrix.of_apply]`, `exact contDiff_const.add (ContDiff.inner ℝ (ContinuousLinearMap.apply ℝ (Rn ℓ) (EuclideanSpace.single a (1:ℝ))).contDiff (ContinuousLinearMap.apply ℝ (Rn ℓ) (EuclideanSpace.single b (1:ℝ))).contDiff)`. - Determinant: `simp only [Matrix.det_apply, Units.smul_def, zsmul_eq_mul]; refine ContDiff.sum (fun σ _ => ?_); exact contDiff_const.mul (contDiff_prod (fun i _ => hentry _ _))`. - Finish with `hdet.sqrt (fun P => (Submission.dohr_eb_ail_gram_det_pos n ℓ P).ne')`.
proof_key_steps:
each entry P -> delta_ab +

is C^infinity (evaluation maps and the inner product)
D(P) = det(I + G(P)) is C^infinity by the Leibniz formula, finite sums and products
D(P) > 0 for all P by gram_det_pos
J = sqrt o D is C^infinity by ContDiff.sqrt

subproblems.title: Second derivative of a C^2 function along a line
subproblems.statement: Let E be a real normed space (E : Type with NormedAddCommGroup E and NormedSpace ℝ E) and F : E -> R of class C^2 (ContDiff ℝ 2 F). Then for all x, v in E, the real function g(t) = F(x + t v) satisfies deriv (deriv g) 0 = D^2F(x)[v][v], where D^2F(x)[v][v] = fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ F) x v v.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ {E : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] (F : E → ℝ), ContDiff ℝ 2 F → ∀ x v : E, deriv (deriv (fun t : ℝ => F (x + t • v))) 0 = fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ F) x v v
subproblems.natural_proof:
1. Regularity. F is C^2 and 2 != 0, so F is differentiable everywhere. Since 1 + 1 <= 2, the derivative map DF = fderiv ℝ F : E -> (E →L[ℝ] ℝ) is C^1 (ContDiff.fderiv_right), hence differentiable everywhere.

2. The line. gamma(t) := x + t v satisfies gamma'(t) = v for every t in R.

3. First derivative of g. By the chain rule, for every t, g has derivative DF(x + t v)[v] = fderiv ℝ F (x + t v) v at t. So the function deriv g equals t -> fderiv ℝ F (x + t v) v for all t.

4. Second derivative. By the chain rule again, the curve t -> DF(x + t v) in E →L[ℝ] ℝ has derivative D(DF)(gamma(0))[gamma'(0)] = fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ F) x v at t = 0, since gamma(0) = x + 0 v = x. Evaluation at the fixed vector v is a continuous linear map (E →L[ℝ] ℝ) -> R. Equivalently, apply the product rule to the pairing of this operator-valued curve with the constant curve v, whose derivative is 0. Hence t -> DF(x + t v) v has derivative (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ F) x v) v at 0.

5. Conclusion. By steps 3 and 4, deriv (deriv g) 0 = deriv (t -> fderiv ℝ F (x + t v) v) 0 = fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ F) x v v. QED

Source: the chain-rule part of parent step 4 (f''(t) = D^2J(tQ)[Q][Q] along t -> tQ), stated for a general C^2 function and base point.

subproblems.title: Second derivative of sqrt(det(I + t^2 S)) at 0 equals tr S
subproblems.statement: For every natural number n and every real n x n matrix S, the function f(t) = sqrt(det(I_n + t^2 S)) (t in R) satisfies deriv (deriv f) 0 = trace S.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ S : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ, deriv (deriv (fun t : ℝ => Real.sqrt (Matrix.det ((1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) + t ^ 2 • S)))) 0 = Matrix.trace S
subproblems.natural_proof:
Notation: tau := trace S. For a polynomial R in R[X], R' is its derivative and R(u) its value at u.

1. Expansion. By Matrix.det_one_add_smul, det(I + r S) = 1 + tau r + R(r) r^2 for every r in R, where R := (det(1 + X • S.map C)).divX.divX is a fixed real polynomial. With r = t^2: p(t) := det(I + t^2 S) = 1 + tau t^2 + R(t^2) t^4 for every t, and f(t) = sqrt(p(t)).

2. First derivative of p. p is differentiable at every t with p'(t) = 2 tau t + R'(t^2) (2t) t^4 + R(t^2) (4 t^3). This uses the chain rule for t -> R(t^2) (derivative R'(t^2) * 2t), the power rule, and the product and sum rules.

3. Second derivative of p at 0. p' is differentiable at 0 with p''(0) = 2 tau:
- 2 tau t has derivative 2 tau;
- u(t) t^4 with u(t) = R'(t^2) 2t has derivative u'(0) * 0^4 + u(0) * 4 * 0^3 = 0 at 0;
- w(t) * 4t^3 with w(t) = R(t^2) has derivative w'(0) * 4 * 0^3 + w(0) * 12 * 0^2 = 0 at 0.
The last two use the product rule with u, w differentiable.

4. Values at 0. p(0) = 1 and p'(0) = 0.

5. Localization. p is continuous at 0 (it is differentiable) and p(0) = 1 > 0, so p > 0 on a neighbourhood U of 0. For t in U, f = sqrt o p is differentiable at t with f'(t) = p'(t) / (2 sqrt(p(t))) (derivative of sqrt at a positive point). So deriv f agrees on U with g(t) := p'(t) / (2 sqrt(p(t))). A derivative at a point depends only on the function near that point, so deriv (deriv f) 0 = g'(0) (Filter.EventuallyEq.deriv_eq).

6. Quotient rule. d(t) := 2 sqrt(p(t)) is differentiable at 0 with d(0) = 2 sqrt(1) = 2 != 0 and d'(0) = 2 p'(0) / (2 sqrt(p(0))) = 0. So g'(0) = (p''(0) d(0) - p'(0) d'(0)) / d(0)^2 = (2 tau * 2 - 0) / 4 = tau.

7. Conclusion. deriv (deriv f) 0 = tau = trace S. QED

Source: parent step 3. There, det(I + sS) = 1 + s tr S + s^2 r(s) (Matrix.det_one_add_smul), phi(s) = sqrt(det(I + sS)), f(t) = phi(t^2) and f''(0) = 2 phi'(0) = tr S. Here the same computation is done directly on p(t) = det(I + t^2 S).

near 0, deriv f = p' / (2 sqrt p) because p > 0 there

subproblems.title: Hessian of the area integrand at 0 is the Hilbert-Schmidt form
subproblems.statement:
For all natural numbers n, l and every Q in L(R^n, R^l) (Q : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ): let J(P) = sqrt(det(I_n + G(P))), with G(P)_{ab} =

and e_a = EuclideanSpace.single a 1. Then D^2J(0)[Q][Q] = fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ J) 0 Q Q = sum_{a in Fin n} ||Q e_a||^2.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ n ℓ : ℕ, ∀ Q : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ, fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ (fun P : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ => Real.sqrt (Matrix.det ((1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) + Matrix.of fun a b : Fin n => inner ℝ (P (EuclideanSpace.single a (1 : ℝ))) (P (EuclideanSpace.single b (1 : ℝ))))))) 0 Q Q = ∑ a : Fin n, ‖Q (EuclideanSpace.single a (1 : ℝ))‖ ^ 2
subproblems.natural_proof:
Notation: fix n, l, Q. L := Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ, J is the area integrand, and S := G(Q) is the n x n matrix S_{ab} = <Q e_a, Q e_b>.

1. J is C^2. By the sibling integrand_smooth (Submission.dohr_eb_ail_contDiff), J is C^infinity on L, hence C^2 (2 <= infinity).

2. Reduction to a line. Apply the sibling line_second_deriv (Submission.dohr_eb_ail_line_second_deriv) with E = L, F = J, x = 0, v = Q: fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ J) 0 Q Q = deriv (deriv (t -> J(0 + t Q))) 0.

3. Scaling of the Gram matrix. For t in R and a in Fin n, (0 + t Q) e_a = t (Q e_a). So G(0 + t Q)_{ab} = <t Q e_a, t Q e_b> = t^2 <Q e_a, Q e_b> = (t^2 S)_{ab}. Hence J(0 + t Q) = sqrt(det(I + t^2 S)) for every t, i.e. the two functions of t are equal.

4. One-variable computation. By the sibling sqrt_det_second_deriv (Submission.dohr_eb_ail_sqrt_det_second_deriv) applied to S: deriv (deriv (t -> sqrt(det(I + t^2 S)))) 0 = trace S.

5. Trace. trace S = sum_a S_{aa} = sum_a <Q e_a, Q e_a> = sum_a ||Q e_a||^2.

Combining steps 2-5: fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ J) 0 Q Q = sum_a ||Q e_a||^2. QED

Source: parent steps 3-4.

subproblems.title: Squared operator norm is at most the squared Hilbert-Schmidt norm
subproblems.statement: For all natural numbers m, k and every continuous linear map Q : R^m -> R^k (Q : Rn m →L[ℝ] Rn k), ||Q||^2 <= sum_{a in Fin m} ||Q e_a||^2, where ||Q|| is the operator norm and e_a = EuclideanSpace.single a 1.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ m k : ℕ, ∀ Q : Rn m →L[ℝ] Rn k, ‖Q‖ ^ 2 ≤ ∑ a : Fin m, ‖Q (EuclideanSpace.single a (1 : ℝ))‖ ^ 2
subproblems.natural_proof:
Put s := sqrt(sum_a ||Q e_a||^2) >= 0.

1. Expansion. Every h in R^m satisfies h = sum_a h_a e_a, so by linearity Q h = sum_a h_a Q e_a.

2. Pointwise bound. By the triangle inequality and homogeneity of the norm, ||Q h|| <= sum_a |h_a| ||Q e_a||. By Cauchy-Schwarz for finite sums, sum_a |h_a| ||Q e_a|| <= sqrt(sum_a |h_a|^2) sqrt(sum_a ||Q e_a||^2) = ||h|| s, since the Euclidean norm is ||h|| = sqrt(sum_a |h_a|^2).

3. Operator norm. ||Q h|| <= s ||h|| for all h and s >= 0, so ||Q|| <= s (ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound).

4. Squaring. Since 0 <= ||Q|| <= s, ||Q||^2 <= s^2 = sum_a ||Q e_a||^2 (the sum is nonnegative, so sqrt squares back to it). QED

subproblems.title: Local uniform continuity of the second derivative of a C^2 function
subproblems.statement: Let E be a real normed space (E : Type with NormedAddCommGroup E and NormedSpace ℝ E) and F : E -> R of class C^2 (ContDiff ℝ 2 F). For every x0 in E and every delta > 0 there is eps > 0 such that, for all x in E with ||x - x0|| <= eps and all Q, Q' in E, |D^2F(x)[Q][Q'] - D^2F(x0)[Q][Q']| <= delta (||Q|| ||Q'||), where D^2F(x)[Q][Q'] = fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ F) x Q Q'.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ {E : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] (F : E → ℝ), ContDiff ℝ 2 F → ∀ x₀ : E, ∀ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ → ∃ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε ∧ ∀ x : E, ‖x - x₀‖ ≤ ε → ∀ Q Q' : E, |fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ F) x Q Q' - fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ F) x₀ Q Q'| ≤ δ * (‖Q‖ * ‖Q'‖)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Write H(x) := fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ F) x, an element of the normed space E →L[ℝ] (E →L[ℝ] ℝ) of bounded bilinear forms with the operator norm.

1. Continuity of H. F is C^2, so DF = fderiv ℝ F is C^1 (ContDiff.fderiv_right, since 1 + 1 <= 2). Hence its derivative H is continuous (ContDiff.continuous_fderiv, as 1 != 0).

2. Choice of eps. By continuity of H at x0 there is r > 0 with ||H(x) - H(x0)|| < delta whenever dist(x, x0) = ||x - x0|| < r. Put eps := r/2 > 0. If ||x - x0|| <= eps then ||x - x0|| < r, so ||H(x) - H(x0)|| < delta.

3. Bilinear estimate. Let B := H(x) - H(x0). For all Q, Q': B Q Q' = H(x) Q Q' - H(x0) Q Q', since subtraction of continuous linear maps is pointwise (applied twice). Also |B Q Q'| <= ||B|| ||Q|| ||Q'|| (ContinuousLinearMap.le_opNorm₂).

4. Conclusion. For ||x - x0|| <= eps and all Q, Q': |H(x) Q Q' - H(x0) Q Q'| <= ||H(x) - H(x0)|| ||Q|| ||Q'|| <= delta (||Q|| ||Q'||). QED
